chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I say Bismillah upon the food?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the vessels are different, say Bismillah upon each vessel.' I said, 'And if I forget to say Bismillah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say, Bismillah upon its first and its last.'
ai.seo_question: How to handle Bismillah when eating from multiple dishes or if one forgets to say it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the practical jurisprudence of *Tasmiyah* (naming Allah) during meals, emphasizing the distinct sanctity of each vessel to ensure continuous divine remembrance. It provides a specific remedial measure for forgetfulness, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease and continuity in worship, as articulated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). This ruling underscores the spiritual significance of mindfulness (*Muraqabah*) throughout the entire act of eating, not merely at the onset.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dawood who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘How shall I Name (Bismillah) upon the meal?’ So heasws said: ‘When there are different vessels, so Name (Bismillah) upon each vessel’. I said, ‘So if I forget to Name (Bismillah)?’ Heasws said: ‘You should be saying, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj upon its first and its last’.
en.sarwar: 20. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Dawud ibn Farqad who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about how I should mention the name of Allah on food. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the dishes are more than one, then you should mention the name of Allah on each one.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if I forget mentioning the name of Allah?’ He (the Imam) told me to say, ‘In the name of Allah at its beginning and at its end.’”
